title: Chennai housewife earns by filming chores for robot training data #tesla #aichoretraining #robotics
description:
A housewife in Tamil Nadu earned 250 rupees an hour by filming herself performing everyday household chores for AI training data. Companies like Tesla and Figure rely on millions of hours of this first-person footage to teach home robots fine motor skills like folding clothes and handling delicate objects, tasks still difficult for machines.

This emerging industry is quietly transforming global labor, turning ordinary actions into valuable AI training inputs. India’s large workforce and low costs have positioned it as a key hub, reflecting a wider trend where humans effectively train robots by doing simple tasks themselves. This shift underscores a new paradigm in automation where human labor supports robotic learning instead of direct replacement.

The demand for realistic human task data drives investment in wearable cameras and smart glasses worldwide, linking everyday workers to cutting-edge AI development. The result is a rapidly growing market where humans and robots collaborate indirectly, advancing home automation capabilities while generating income through data collection.
